source.title: Probing Knowledge Recovery in Unlearned Models

record.file_problem: none; the full post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery after unlearning with refusal-direction ablation, forget-set representation-direction ablation, and unrelated fine-tuning; these are conceptual tests of the recovery claim.
record.gate_note: The post cites findings from other work on knowledge recovery, but those cited results are not recorded as rows. It reports that some refusal-direction experiments could not be interpreted or performed meaningfully because no clean direction was available or checkpoints were degenerate. It reports testing four loss-based methods across 16 layer and pooling configurations each, but does not give the per-configuration results; best-recovery figures are recorded only where stated.
record.test_reason: The post applies three recovery probes to six existing WMDP-Bio-unlearned Llama-3-8B-Instruct checkpoints and reports WMDP-Bio accuracy before and after each: refusal-direction ablation, forget-set representation-direction ablation (a replication of Arditi & Chughtai), and GSM8K fine-tuning. These results bear directly on versions A, B and C.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right. The authors also stress three points. A single probe is insufficient because different probes reveal different residual access. WMDP forced-choice accuracy overstates recovery, since only 40–47% of recovered answers showed genuine reasoning. GradDiff's SFT gain likely reflects restored general capability rather than recovered knowledge.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates existing unlearned checkpoints using three recovery probes rather than testing one original unlearning recipe; uses GSM8K for unrelated fine-tuning and two types of activation-direction ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery differed by probe and unlearning method. Refusal-direction ablation gave no WMDP recovery for the only checkpoint with a clean direction; representation-direction ablation and GSM8K fine-tuning produced method-dependent results. Four loss-based methods were tried across 16 layer and pooling configurations each, but per-configuration outcomes are not reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning lowered refusal rates on unrelated harmful prompts: IDK-AP refused 0% versus 98% for the base model, and RMU's refusal was also lower. NPO and NPO-ILU became degenerate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning methods degrade unrelated safety behaviours such as refusal, and general coherence.

fits_no_version.finding: GSM8K SFT changed MMLU, with a +29.8 rise for GradDiff from a near-chance 24.9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some unlearned checkpoints lose general ability, and unrelated fine-tuning restores it.

fits_no_version.finding: Only 40–47% of flipped answers had genuine supporting reasoning, and contradiction was also present in stable-correct answers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forced-choice WMDP recovery overstates recovery of usable knowledge.

record.problems: Only six Llama-3-8B-Instruct unlearned checkpoints were tested. GSM8K was the sole unrelated fine-tuning dataset. The qualitative evaluation used small samples, and the NPO and NPO-ILU checkpoints produced incoherent text, complicating interpretation of benchmark recovery. Per-configuration ablation results are not provided.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified refusal-rate outcomes for the other checkpoints are included because the post says those tests were not clean or meaningful and does not give exact rates, except the stated qualitative cases. MMLU results are recorded, but linked to none of the recovery versions because MMLU does not measure recovered targeted knowledge.

untested.parts: General ability is compared with the base model only through MMLU numbers; there is no formal preservation test. Only Llama-3-8B-Instruct checkpoints were tested.
Only GSM8K was used. Loosely related data and fine-tuning on a subset of the forgotten facts were not tested.
Only refusal directions and forget-set mean-difference directions were tested. There is no direct analysis of blocking versus deletion beyond these probes.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information were not tested.

missing.what: MMLU stayed flat for all methods after forget-representation ablation (no values given)
Base Llama-3-8B-Instruct WMDP-Bio accuracy of 73.2%, the reference point for the gap-recovery figures
The SFT control (matched fine-tuning of base Llama) is described, but its results are not reported
A smaller unblinded qualitative evaluation after SFT showed a similar pattern

record.verdict_notes: The checkpoints come from others (ScaleAI, OPTML-Group); none of the original sources is this study. Some checkpoints do not meet A's premise of preserved general ability: GradDiff's MMLU is 24.9 and NPO/NPO-ILU are degenerate, so recovery results on them say little about A. This is a LessWrong post from a BlueDot sprint and is not peer reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare the checkpoints’ general ability with a stated pre-unlearning baseline, and does not establish that all current unlearning methods or simple attacks behave this way.
Tests GSM8K as the unrelated fine-tuning set only; does not test other unrelated or loosely related data or fine-tuning on a subset of forgotten facts.
Tests refusal-direction and forget-set representation-direction ablation; does not test other internal edits or establish a general mechanism across methods.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
No newer counter-method claiming resistance to these attacks is tested.

tranche.reason: Different recovery probes on existing checkpoints, aimed at the same question. One probe replicates Arditi & Chughtai, which is not an original.

source_check.notes: SFT control (matched fine-tuning on base Llama) described, results not given. The only uncertainty is the Probe 1 95% CI; the ablation and SFT tables are point estimates. Rows r4/r5/r12 are 'observed' at 57-61% of the gap; r13 recovers 48% on an incoherent NPO checkpoint. Only 40-47% of flipped answers show genuine reasoning (small, partly unblinded samples).

statements.correction: ILU-RMU refusal-direction ablation: WMDP-Bio not recovered. The 95% CI excluded improvements larger than 1.4 pp. Matched-control and random-control ablations were also null.
statements.problem: 'with the 95% CI excluding improvement' overstates the result. The CI excluded only improvements larger than 1.4 pp.
